content:
Consideration was given to the Procurement and
Contracts Report, which sought Cabinet approval for the procurement
and award of the contracts listed in Appendix 2, provided an
overview of current and planned procurement activity, updated
Cabinet on progress since the previous report, and established the
basis for publication of the Council’s procurement pipeline
in line with the National Procurement Policy Statement and the
Procurement Act 2023.
 
RESOLVED:
i)                
Cabinet agreed to defer making a
decision on this matter to a future meeting to allow further
time for consideration and consultation with services on the
information presented.
topline: The Council has decided to defer the decision on procurement and award of contracts for further consideration and consultation.

content:
Consideration was given to the NewcastleGateshead Local Plan report, which set out
the proposed approach to preparing a new joint Local Plan with
Newcastle City Council, reported progress to date, sought approval
to issue the Notice of Intention and publish the Local Plan
timetable, proposed governance arrangements to oversee plan
preparation, and enabled early consultation, evidence development
and delegated progression of the Plan through the statutory
gateways before future reports back to Cabinet and Council ahead of
submission for examination.
 
RESOLVED:
i)                
That the issuing and publication of the Notices of Intention by 30
June 2026, and progression through Gateway 1 by 31 October 2026,
which commences the 30-month Local Plan preparation process, be
approved.
ii)               
That publication of the Local Plan timetable be approved.
iii)             
That delegated authority be granted to the Strategic Director for
Economy, Innovation and Growth and the Chief Legal Officer of Legal
and Democratic Services, in consultation with the Portfolio Holder,
to progress preparation of the Local Plan through the statutory
gateways.
iv)             
That the governance arrangements, including the establishment of a
Joint Member Steering Group and a Joint Member Panel to oversee
preparation of the Local Plan, be approved.
v)              
That early scoping consultation in relation to the Communications
and Engagement Strategy and the Scope of the Local Plan be
approved.
vi)             
That progression of the evidence base for the Local Plan be
approved, and delegated authority be granted to the Strategic
Director for Economy, Innovation and Growth, in consultation with
the Portfolio Holder, to publish evidence studies and
assessments.
 
The above decision was made for the following
reasons:
 
a)            
To progress the development of Gateshead’s Local Plan as
required by government policy and statutory obligations under the
Planning and Compulsory Purchase Act 2004, the Localism Act 2011
and the Town and Country Planning (Local Planning) (England)
Regulations 2026.
topline: The Gateshead Council has decided to approve the preparation of a new joint Local Plan with Newcastle City Council.

content:
Consideration was given to the report on
Appointments to Advisory Groups, Other Bodies of the Council, Joint
Committees and Outside Bodies, which presented the nominations of
the Reform, Liberal Democrat, Labour and Green Groups.
 
Cabinet was asked to consider nominations so
that appointments could be made to the relevant advisory groups,
partnerships, joint committees, outside bodies and youth and
community organisations for the municipal year.
 
The following Labour appointments were
presented at the meeting verbally via the Monitoring Officer:
 
Local Bus Board for Gateshead – Cllr S
Edge
Corporate Parenting Board – Cllr K
Henderson
Joint Bridges Committee – Cllr S
Gibson
Mountsett
Crematorium Committee – Cllr K McCartney
Tyne & Wear Trading Standards Joint
Committee – Cllr C Buckley
Greenside Community Association – Cllrs
S Edge and K McCartney
Chopwell Community
Association – Cllrs M McNestry and L Caffrey
Blackhall Mill Community Association –
Cllr L Caffrey
Path Head Quarry Liaison Group – Cllr K
McCartney
 
RESOLVED:
i)                
That the nominations of the Reform, Liberal Democrat, Labour and
Green Groups be agreed.

 
The above decision was made for the following
reasons:
 
a)                
To ensure that the views of the political groups are considered
when the appointments are made.
b)                
To ensure that the most appropriate Councillors are appointed to
each body.
topline: The Council has decided to approve nominations from various political groups for appointments to advisory groups and outside bodies.

content:
Nominations were sought for the Leader of the
Metropolitan Borough of Gateshead.
 
Councillor S Campion seconded by Councillor F
Pearce, moved that Councillor N Allan be appointed as Leader.
 
The proposed nomination was put to a vote.
 
COUNCIL RESOLVED:
 
(i)           
Councillor N Allan be elected Leader of the Metropolitan Borough of
Gateshead for a period of four years.
topline: The Council has decided to appoint Councillor N Allan as the Leader of the Metropolitan Borough of Gateshead.

That the press and public be excluded from the meeting during

content:
Consideration was given to the adoption of
Gateshead’s Community Cohesion Strategy 2026–2031,
which sets out a borough-wide framework for strengthening community
connections, reducing harm and tensions, promoting fair access to
services, and supporting local leadership. The report sought
Cabinet approval of the Strategy, taking account of public
consultation findings and confirming a coordinated approach to
improving community safety, inclusion and wellbeing across the
borough.
 
RESOLVED:
i)                
Cabinet approved the Community Cohesion Strategy 2026–2031
for implementation.
ii)               
Cabinet agreed that the Community Cohesion Group will oversee
delivery, monitoring and reporting to the Safer Gateshead
Partnership.
iii)             
Cabinet approved the development of a detailed action plan aligned
with the Strategy’s five priorities.
 
The above decision was made for the following
reasons:
a)                
To establish a clear, evidence-based approach to building stronger,
safer and more connected communities.
b)                
To ensure coordinated delivery and strengthen community leadership
and partnership.
topline: The council has decided to approve Gateshead's Community Cohesion Strategy 2026-2031 for implementation.

content:
Consideration was given to the submission of
the MetroGreen Area Action Plan for independent examination. The
report sought Cabinet approval to progress the Area Action Plan as
part of Gateshead’s Local Plan, including noting consultation
outcomes, authorising submission to the Secretary of State and
enabling the examination process to proceed.
 
RESOLVED:
i)                
Cabinet noted the Consultation Statement April 2026, which includes
proposed minor modifications, as set out in Appendix 2.
ii)               
Cabinet authorised formal submission of the MetroGreen Area Action
Plan Local Plan document, as set out in Appendix 3, and associated
submission documentation to the Secretary of State pursuant to
Regulation 22 of the Town and Country Planning (Local Planning)
(England) Regulations 2012.
iii)             
Cabinet granted authority to the Inspector appointed to hold the
public examination to make modifications to the MetroGreen Area
Action Plan Submission Document under Section 20(7C) of the
Planning and Compulsory Purchase Act 2004, as amended.
iv)             
Cabinet delegated authority to the Service Director for Climate
Change, Compliance, Planning and Transport and the Strategic
Director of Legal and Corporate Services, in consultation with the
relevant Cabinet Member, to make changes to the MetroGreen Area
Action Plan and supporting documentation, prepare and give evidence
in support of the examination and carry out consultation on any
modifications recommended by the Planning Inspector.
 
The above decision was made for the following
reason:
a)                
To progress the development of Gateshead’s Local Plan as
required by government policy and statutory obligations under the
Planning and Compulsory Purchase Act 2004, the Localism Act 2011
and the Town and Country Planning (Local Plans) Regulations 2012,
as amended.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to approve the progress of the MetroGreen Area Action Plan as part of Gateshead's Local Plan.

content:
Consideration was given to the approval of the
School Term Dates for the 2027/28 academic year, enabling schools,
parents and stakeholders to plan effectively. The report sought
Cabinet agreement to the proposed calendar, which aligns with
neighbouring local authorities and statutory requirements.
 
RESOLVED:
i)                
Cabinet agreed the dates set out in the School Term Dates for
2027/28 as attached to the report.

 
The above decision was made for the following
reason:
a)                
To allow future planning to take place.
b)                
To make effective and efficient use of Local Authority
resources.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to approve School Term Dates for the 2027/28 academic year.

content:
Consideration was given to the approval of
revised Corporate Guidance and Procedures under the Regulation of
Investigatory Powers Act 2000, updated to reflect non RIPA
surveillance activity and minor administrative amendments. The
report sought Cabinet approval to ensure investigations continue to
be conducted lawfully and proportionately.
 
RESOLVED:
i)                
Cabinet approved the amended Regulation of Investigatory Powers
Corporate Guidance and Procedures as set out in Appendix 1.

 
The above decision was made for the following
reason:
 
a)                
To ensure the Council has an up to date and accurate procedure to
safeguard individuals and communities while avoiding unnecessary
infringement of human rights.
topline: The Council has decided to approve revised Corporate Guidance and Procedures under the Regulation of Investigatory Powers Act 2000.

content:
Consideration was given to granting
retrospective approval to the Council’s response to the
national consultation on the Fair Pay for Care Workers proposals.
The report sought Cabinet endorsement of the submission, which
supports fair pay arrangements for care workers and recognises the
importance of the care sector.
 
RESOLVED:
i)                
Cabinet retrospectively approved the Council’s response to
the national Fair Pay for Care Workers consultation, as
submitted.

 
The above decision was made for the following
reason:
a)                
The Fair Pay agreement for Care Workers is in line with the
Council’s Thrive strategic approach
topline: The Council has decided to retrospectively approve their response to the national consultation on Fair Pay for Care Workers proposals.

content:
Consideration was given to the progress made
in preparing the South of Tyne and Wear Local Nature Recovery
Strategy and the next steps required to move towards adoption. The
report sought Cabinet agreement to proposed updates following
consultation and to commence the statutory confirmation period with
Supporting Authorities.
 
RESOLVED:
i)                
Cabinet noted the progress made in preparing the South of Tyne and
Wear Local Nature Recovery Strategy.
ii)               
Cabinet approved the proposed updates to the draft Strategy, as set
out in the Schedule of Changes, and agreed to begin the 28 day
statutory period with Supporting Authorities.
iii)             
Cabinet delegated authority to the Service Director for Climate
Change, Compliance, Planning and Transport, in consultation with
the relevant Cabinet Member, to adopt and publish the final
Strategy once confirmation is received from all Supporting
Authorities, and to make any minor, non material changes prior to
publication.
 
The above decision was made for the following
reasons:
a)                
To ensure compliance with the Environment Act 2021 and progress the
Strategy to adoption and publication.
b)                
To allow flexibility to address final technical refinements without
unnecessary delay.
topline: The UK council has approved updates to the South of Tyne and Wear Local Nature Recovery Strategy.

content:
Consideration was given to proposals to
simplify and strengthen the trading governance arrangements for
North East Museums. The report sought Cabinet approval to establish
a single combined trading company to replace existing arrangements,
improving efficiency and governance.
 
RESOLVED:
i)                
Cabinet approved the proposal to create a single combined trading
company for North East Museums.
 
The above decision was made for the following
reason:
a)                
To ensure efficient and effective governance of North East
Museums.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to establish a single combined trading company for North East Museums.

content:
Consideration was given to the introduction of
a new Behaviour Framework to underpin the Council’s refreshed
Corporate Values, previously approved by Full Council. The report
sought Cabinet agreement to recommend adoption of the Framework to
Full Council, ensuring values are translated into clear, practical
and measurable behaviours to support a positive organisational
culture and high performance.
 
RESOLVED:
i)                
Cabinet agreed to recommend to Full Council the Behaviour Framework
that will underpin the Council’s refreshed Corporate
Values.

 
The above decision was made for the following
reasons:
 
a)                
To ensure the Council’s values and behaviour framework
reflects current needs and strategic priorities.
b)                
To ensure the corporate values and behaviours are relevant,
meaningful and resonate with employees and stakeholders.
c)                
To support the development of a positive organisational culture,
differentiate the Council as an employer and strengthen attraction
and retention of talented individuals.
d)                
To ensure the behaviour framework aligns with the Values and sets
out how people are expected to behave and not behave.
topline: The Council has decided to introduce a new Behaviour Framework to support its refreshed Corporate Values.

content:
Consideration was given to the acquisition of
land at Coalburns to deliver woodland creation, support
biodiversity, carbon sequestration, climate resilience and public
access. The report sought approval in principle for the land
purchase, subject to grant funding, and delegation of authority to
complete the transaction.
 
RESOLVED – That, having considered a
report in the absence of the press and public pursuant to Schedule
12A of the Local Government Act 1972 (as amended), Cabinet:
 
i)                
Agreed in principle to the Council purchasing the subject property
for a price in line with the Council’s valuation, subject to
grant funding being confirmed in writing.
ii)               
Cabinet agreed to fund the purchase of the existing woodland and
watercourse from existing Council budgets.
iii)             
Cabinet delegated authority to the Strategic Director of Economy,
Innovation and Growth and the Strategic Director of Resources and
Digital, in consultation with the Cabinet Member for Environment
and Transport, to agree terms and complete the purchase.
iv)             
Cabinet delegated authority to the Strategic Director of Economy,
Innovation and Growth and the Strategic Director of Resources and
Digital, in consultation with the Cabinet Member for Environment
and Transport, to accept the grant from North East Community
Forest.
 
The above decision was made for the following
reasons:
a)                
To support the Council’s commitment to tree planting and
woodland creation targets.
b)                
To contribute to nature recovery and demonstrate compliance with
the enhanced Biodiversity Duty.
topline: The Council has decided to acquire land at Coalburns for woodland creation and biodiversity support.

content:
Consideration was given to the new Post 16
Education Strategy, including the consultation process and
arrangements for final approval. The report aimed to secure Cabinet
endorsement of the Strategy, which promotes a place based approach
to post 16 education to improve participation, employment outcomes,
health and wellbeing for residents.
 
RESOLVED:
i)                
Cabinet recommended to Council approval of the implementation of
the Post 16 Strategy.

 
The above decision was made for the following
reason:
a)                
To demonstrate the Council’s commitment to improving the
lives of residents through post 16 education.
b)                
To drive a place based approach to education planning.
topline: The Council has decided to recommend approval of the implementation of the Post 16 Education Strategy.

content:
Consideration was given to the report which
asked Cabinet to review the draft organisational structures,
consider the rationale for the proposed changes, note the use of
the Decision Making Accountability approach to inform the design,
and recommend that the draft structures be taken forward for
Council consideration, thereby initiating the statutory redundancy
and collective consultation process, with the pay protection policy
applied where appropriate.
 
RESOLVED – That, having considered a
report in the absence of the press and public pursuant to Schedule
12A of the Local Government Act 1972 (as amended):
i)                
Cabinet agreed to recommend to Council that the changes suggested
to Council Group Structures, as set out by the Corporate Management
Team, be taken forward as a proposed structure to be consulted on
in line with the relevant Redundancy Collective Consultation
regulations.
ii)               
Cabinet agreed to recommend to Council that the organisation
commences a minimum 45?day collective
consultation on 20 March 2026 on the proposed organisational
changes.
iii)             
Cabinet agreed to recommend to Council that the Pay Protection
policy be applied to any employee who takes up an alternative role
in the organisation, on a lesser salary/terms and conditions due to
a decision taken by the Council, regardless of grade or position,
for the purposes of this exercise and any other moving forward.
 
The above decision was made for the following
reasons:

a)    
To allow the reorganisation of the Council to proceed and build a
structure that will deliver benefits for residents, employees,
stakeholders and partners.

b)    
To ensure equity in the application of the pay protection
policy.
topline: The Council has decided to reorganise its structure and implement a pay protection policy for employees affected by the changes.

content:
Consideration was given to the report which
sought agreement to the updated Gateshead Joint Health and
Wellbeing Strategy, titled Good jobs, homes, health and friends,
and to recommend that Council adopt the Strategy as part of its
policy framework, ensuring it reflects recent social and economic
challenges, incorporates additional Marmot principles, and
continues to guide collective action to reduce health inequalities
across the borough.
 
RESOLVED:
i)                
Cabinet agreed the updated Health and Wellbeing Strategy subject to
approval by Council.
ii)               
Cabinet renewed their shared commitment to the vision of the Joint
Health and Wellbeing Strategy and to delivering the eight strategic
objectives, together with the ways of working set out in the
Strategy.
iii)             
Cabinet supported the development of an evaluative framework which
identifies short, medium and long?term
measures in working towards becoming a Marmot place.
iv)             
Cabinet supported a Health and Wellbeing Board stakeholder workshop
to develop the delivery mechanisms for each policy objective,
strengthening accountability and defining roles and
responsibilities for each partner.
 
The above decision was made for the following
reasons:
a)                
To ensure the Council is well placed to respond to the health and
wellbeing needs of the borough, alongside taking action to tackle
increasing health inequalities within Gateshead.
b)                
To ensure that the Council and the Health and Wellbeing Board are
well placed to meet their responsibilities as required by the
Health and Social Care Act 2012 and associated regulations.
topline: The Council has decided to adopt the updated Gateshead Joint Health and Wellbeing Strategy to tackle health inequalities in the borough.

content:
Consideration was given to the report which
sought approval of Gateshead’s Culture Strategy, Creative
Places, together with its three?year delivery
plan, setting out a ten?year vision for
culture in Gateshead and establishing culture as a driver for
economic growth, health and wellbeing, placemaking and community
identity across the borough.
 
RESOLVED:
i)                
Cabinet approved and recommended to Council the Gateshead Culture
Strategy and Delivery Plan Creative Places.
ii)               
Cabinet approved the development of an expression of interest for
Gateshead to bid for UK Town of Culture 2028.
 
The above decision was made for the following
reasons:
a)                
To ensure that culture is embedded in the Council’s
strategies, including the Health and Wellbeing Strategy and the
Corporate Plan.
b)                
To support delivery of the four pillars of the strategy, focusing
on civic and community leadership, identity and pride in place,
economy, and health and wellbeing.
topline: The Council has decided to approve Gateshead's Culture Strategy and Creative Places, setting a ten-year vision for culture as a driver for economic growth, health and wellbeing.

content:
Consideration was given to the report which
sought approval for the transfer of uncollectable Council Tax and
Non?Domestic Rates balances where all
appropriate recovery action had been taken and the outstanding
amounts were considered irrecoverable, in order to ensure that the
Council’s financial records accurately
reflect the true position.
 
RESOLVED:
i)                
Cabinet agreed to the transfer of uncollectable Council Tax
balances amounting to £1,738,983.
ii)               
Cabinet agreed to the transfer of uncollectable Non?Domestic Rates balances amounting to £1,229,782.
iii)             
Cabinet noted the action taken under delegated powers to transfer
uncollectable balances of £2,500 or less.

 
The above decision was made for the following
reasons:
a)                
To ensure the effective management of the Council’s
resources.
b)                
To ensure that the Council’s accounts accurately reflect the
correct financial position.
topline: The Council has decided to transfer uncollectable balances to accurately reflect financial position

content:
Consideration was given to the report which
sought approval for the transfer of uncollectable miscellaneous
income debts and Housing Benefit overpayments, where all
appropriate recovery action had been taken and the outstanding
amounts were considered irrecoverable, in order
to ensure the Council’s accounts accurately reflect
the true financial position.
 
RESOLVED:
i)                
Cabinet agreed to the transfer of uncollectable balances on sundry
debtor accounts amounting to £331,842.
ii)               
Cabinet agreed to the transfer of uncollectable Housing Benefit
overpayment invoices amounting to £115,028.
iii)             
Cabinet noted the action taken under delegated powers to transfer
uncollectable balances of £2,500 or less.
 
The above decision was made for the following
reasons:
a)                
To ensure the effective management of the Council’s
resources.
b)                
To ensure that the Council’s accounts accurately reflect the
correct financial position.
topline: The Council has decided to transfer uncollectable debts and overpayments to accurately reflect its financial position.

content:
Consideration was given to the report which
sought approval for the transfer of uncollectable rent arrears owed
by former tenants and sundry account debts in
excess of £2,500, where all reasonable recovery action
had been taken and the outstanding balances were considered
irrecoverable, to ensure robust debt management and accurate
financial reporting.
 
RESOLVED:
i)                
Cabinet agreed to the transfer of uncollectable balances on former
tenant rent arrears accounts amounting to £419,473.
ii)               
Cabinet agreed to the transfer of uncollectable balances on sundry
account debts amounting to £42,974.
iii)             
Cabinet noted the action taken under delegated powers to transfer
uncollectable balances of £2,500 or less.
 
The above decision was made for the following
reasons:
a)                
All recovery methods have been considered and, where appropriate,
pursued before making the decision to write off the debts.
b)                
Officer time can be maximised on achieving the greatest returns,
while ensuring robust procedures for debt management are in place
across all revenue streams.
topline: The Council has decided to transfer uncollectable rent arrears and sundry account debts exceeding £2,500 for robust debt management and accurate financial reporting.

content:
Consideration was given to the report which
sought approval of the Treasury Policy Statement and Treasury
Strategy for the period 2026/27 to 2030/31, setting out the
framework within which the Council will manage borrowing,
investments, cash flow and treasury risks, and ensuring compliance
with statutory requirements and recognised codes of practice.
 
RESOLVED:
i)                
Cabinet agreed the Treasury Policy Statement and Treasury Strategy
for 2026/27 to 2030/31 and recommended them to Council for
approval.

 
The above decision was made for the following
reasons:
a)                
To ensure the Council fully complies with the requirements of good
financial practice in Treasury Management.
topline: The Council has decided to approve the Treasury Policy Statement and Treasury Strategy for the period 2026/27 to 2030/31.

content:
Consideration was given to the report which
sought agreement to the Pay Policy Statement for 2026–27, as
required by the Localism Act 2011, setting out the Council’s
approach to pay accountability, including the remuneration of
senior officers, the lowest paid employees, pay ratios and
transparency requirements.
 
RESOLVED:
i)                
Cabinet agreed the Pay Policy Statement 2026–27 and
recommended it to Council for approval.

 
The above decision was made for the following
reasons:
a)                
To comply with the requirements of the Localism Act 2011.
topline: The Council has decided to approve the Pay Policy Statement for 2026-27, setting out their approach to pay accountability.

content:
Consideration was given to the Rent Arrears
Prevention and Recovery Policy, which sought approval for a
consolidated and updated policy setting out the Council’s
approach to the prevention, management and recovery of rent arrears
across its council housing stock, supporting tenants to sustain
their tenancies and complementing the existing Rent and Service
Charge Setting Policy.
 
RESOLVED:
i)                
Cabinet agreed to approve the Rent Arrears Prevention and Recovery
Policy.
 
The above decision was made for the following
reasons:
a)                
To accompany the existing Rent and Service Charge Setting
Policy.
b)                
To clearly set out the Council’s approach to the management
of council housing rental income by supporting tenants throughout
their tenancy.
topline: The UK council has decided to approve the Rent Arrears Prevention and Recovery Policy.

content:
Consideration was given to the report which
sought Cabinet approval for a refreshed Tenancy Management Policy
following resident consultation. The revised policy sets out how
the Council manages tenancies from commencement to termination,
including tenancy types, changes, audits, enforcement, decants,
succession and tenancy support, and reflects the Council’s
Thrive agenda, updated legislative requirements and the Regulator
of Social Housing’s Consumer Standards effective from 1 April
2024.
 
RESOLVED:
i)                
Cabinet approved the final Tenancy Management Policy (Appendix
3).
ii)               
Cabinet authorised implementation of the policy from April 2026,
supported by appropriate staff training.
iii)             
Cabinet noted the outcomes of the resident consultation.

 
The above decision was made for the following
reasons:
a)                
To ensure the Council maintains an up?to?date Tenancy Management Policy
that meets regulatory standards.
b)                
To ensure tenancy management practices remain clear, transparent
and supportive of residents.
c)                
To reflect consultation feedback and provide an accessible policy
for tenants.
topline: The Council has approved a new Tenancy Management Policy following resident consultation.

content:
Consideration was given to the report which
sought Cabinet approval for the final version of Gateshead
Council’s updated Tenancy Agreement following statutory
consultation with tenants. The report outlined the consultation
process, key themes arising from engagement, and the proposed
variations required to ensure the Agreement complies with
legislative requirements, regulatory standards and current policy
and operational practice.
 
RESOLVED:
i)                
Cabinet approved the final updated Tenancy Agreement (Appendix 3)
and the steps required for its implementation.
ii)               
Cabinet authorised officers to issue the statutory Notice of
Variation to all Council housing tenants, giving at least four
weeks’ notice.
iii)             
Cabinet approved implementation of the revised Tenancy Agreement
alongside the updated Tenancy Management Policy.
iv)             
Cabinet noted the consultation outcomes and amendments made in
response to resident feedback.
 
The above decision was made for the following
reasons:
a)                
To ensure compliance with statutory requirements and regulatory
standards.
b)                
To provide greater clarity on tenant and landlord responsibilities,
including domestic abuse provisions, tenancy fraud, unsuitable
animals, repairs and data protection.
c)                
To support safe and effective tenancy management across all Council
housing stock.
topline: The Gateshead Council has decided to approve the final updated Tenancy Agreement for Council housing tenants.

content:
Consideration was given to the report which
sought approval to demolish a number of Council?owned garage blocks that are fully void, in poor
condition and no longer considered financially viable to retain, in
order to address issues of cost, safety and under?utilisation and to consider alternative uses of the
sites.
 
RESOLVED:
i)                
Cabinet approved the demolition of the housing garage blocks
identified in the report.

 
The above decision was made for the following
reasons:
a)                
The garages are all in very poor condition and the components have
reached the end of their life cycle.
b)                
Demolition presents an opportunity to provide additional parking
areas.
topline: The Council has decided to approve the demolition of several garage blocks to address cost, safety, and under-utilisation issues.

content:
Consideration was given to the report which
sought approval to extend the current Special Educational Needs and
Disabilities Strategy from 2026 to 2028, to enable continued
delivery of the existing improvement plan, ensure alignment with
inspection activity and consultation feedback, and maintain focus
on the agreed priority areas for children and young people with
SEND.
 
RESOLVED:
i)                
Cabinet agreed to extend the period of the current SEND Strategy to
2028.

 
The above decision was made for the following
reasons:
a)                
To enable the Council to fulfil its pledges against the four
priority areas contained within the SEND Strategy.
b)                
To ensure continuity of delivery in response to consultation
feedback and inspection findings while maintaining focus on
improvement activity.
topline: The Council has decided to extend the Special Educational Needs and Disabilities Strategy to 2028.

content:
Consideration was given to the report which
sought Cabinet approval to allocate grant funding to Citizens
Advice Gateshead for the financial year 2026/27, to enable the
continuation of information, advice and guidance services while a
framework for the structured delivery of such services in Gateshead
is developed, and to support the Council’s approach to
tackling poverty, improving financial resilience and addressing
health inequalities.
 
RESOLVED:
i)                
Cabinet approved the award of grant funding of £1,056,000 to
Citizens Advice Gateshead to enable continuation of services during
2026/27, and authorised the Chief Legal Officer, Corporate Services
and Governance to determine appropriate terms of a grant funding
agreement between the Council and Citizens Advice Gateshead for
this purpose.
ii)               
Cabinet noted the development of the framework for structured
delivery of information, advice and guidance services in Gateshead
and the identification of funding via the Crisis Resilience Fund as
the Council’s investment in resilience services.
 
The above decision was made for the following
reasons:
a)                
To enable the award of funding through provision of a grant
agreement to Citizens Advice Gateshead.
b)                
To support the Council’s appropriate investment of Crisis
Resilience Funding, contributing towards improving the financial
resilience of residents of Gateshead and towards achievement of
outcomes required from the Crisis Resilience Fund, namely
empowering residents to better manage financial shocks and mitigate
the occurrence, recurrence and escalation of crises, and
strengthening resilience networks within local communities,
ensuring there are clear referral pathways between them and crisis
support.
topline: The Council has decided to approve grant funding to Citizens Advice Gateshead for the financial year 2026/27 to support community resilience and tackle poverty.

content:
Consideration was given to the report which
sought approval to redesignate Hill Top Maintained Special School
from providing for pupils with Moderate Learning Difficulties and
Autism to Autism only, in response to increasing demand for
specialist autism provision, to strengthen the Council’s
in?borough offer and ensure effective use of
specialist education resources.
 
RESOLVED:
i)                
Cabinet approved the redesignation of Hill Top Maintained Special
School from Moderate Learning Difficulties and Autism to Autism
only.
ii)               
Cabinet approved the reduction of sixth form places at the school
from seventeen to eight.
iii)             
Cabinet authorised officers to proceed with site development to
ensure the school can fully meet the needs of children with
autism.

 
The above decision was made for the following
reasons:
a)                
To enhance the in?borough offer for children
with autism requiring access to specialist secondary provision.
b)                
To maximise the efficient use of the high needs block for young
people with the most complex needs.
c)                
To ensure that the provision at Hill Top is comparable with other
specialist settings within the borough.
topline: The Council has decided to redesignate Hill Top Maintained Special School to provide for students with autism only, reducing sixth form places and authorizing site development.

content:
Consideration was given to the report which
asked Cabinet to recommend to Council the Corporate Plan Action
Plan for 2026–2027, setting out the key actions the Council
will take over the next year to deliver the Corporate Plan
2025–2030, align strategic priorities with resource and
service planning, and guide activity in response to
borough?wide need.
 
RESOLVED:
i)                
Cabinet recommended that Council agrees the Corporate Plan Action
Plan 2026–2027.

 
The above decision was made for the following
reasons:
a)                
To prioritise and guide the Council’s activity in response to
borough?wide need.
topline: The UK council has decided to approve the Corporate Plan Action Plan for 2026-2027.

content:
Consideration was given to the report which
provided an update and sought approval of a new Domestic Abuse
Housing Policy for the Council housing sector, developed in line
with the Policy Development Framework to ensure compliance with the
Regulator for Social Housing’s Consumer Standards and to set
out the Council’s approach to tackling domestic abuse,
supporting victims and survivors, and holding perpetrators to
account.
 
RESOLVED:
i)                
Cabinet noted that the policy had been shared with Corporate
Management Team, HEHC Portfolio, Domestic Abuse Partnership Board,
Women and Girls Committee and the Director of Public Health.
ii)               
Cabinet approved the Domestic Abuse Policy.
iii)             
Cabinet noted that, following approval of the policy, staff
training will be required to ensure employees are equipped with the
skills and knowledge to apply the policy appropriately, with these
actions identified within the Domestic Abuse Partnership
Board’s action plan and the service plan for 2026/27.

 
The above decision was made for the following
reasons:
a)                
To ensure that the Council is fully compliant with the Regulator
for Social Housing’s Consumer Standards.
b)                
To ensure that appropriate housing?related
responses are provided to victims and survivors of domestic abuse
and their families.
topline: The Council has decided to approve a new Domestic Abuse Housing Policy to support victims and survivors of domestic abuse.

content:
Consideration was given to the report which
sought approval for the disposal of approximately 4.93 hectares
(12.2 acres) of Council?owned land at Church
Place, Brandling, Felling to the
Gateshead Regeneration Partnership (GRP), subject to the grant of
planning permission for the construction of residential dwellings,
including affordable housing.
 
RESOLVED – That, having considered a
report in the absence of the press and public pursuant to Schedule
12A of the Local Government Act 1972 (as amended):
i)                
Cabinet approved the disposal of the land at Church Place,
Brandling, Felling to the Gateshead Regeneration Partnership,
subject to the grant of planning permission for the construction of
131 dwellings.
ii)               
Cabinet approved that the transfer value of the land be determined
in accordance with the development agreement, in consultation with
the Strategic Director of Economy, Innovation and Growth.
 
The above decision was made for the following
reasons:
a)                
Development of vacant land for residential development.
b)                
Provision of new housing within Felling.
topline: The Council has decided to approve the disposal of land for the construction of residential dwellings in Felling.

content:
Consideration was given to the exempt report
which sought approval for the disposal of land at Church Place,
Brandling, Felling to the Gateshead Regeneration Partnership, to
enable redevelopment of the site for residential use and to support
the delivery of new housing as part of the Council’s
regeneration objectives for the area.
 
RESOLVED – That, having considered a
report in the absence of the press and public pursuant to Schedule
12A of the Local Government Act 1972 (as amended):
i)                
Cabinet approved the disposal of the land at Church Place,
Brandling, Felling to the Gateshead Regeneration Partnership,
subject to planning permission being granted for the construction
of 131 dwellings and subject to the transfer value being determined
in accordance with the report.

 
The above decision was made for the following
reasons:
a)                
Development of vacant land for residential development.
b)                
Provision of new housing within Felling.
topline: The council has decided to approve the disposal of land for residential development in Felling.

content:
Consideration was given to the report which
sought approval to submit a Business Case to the North East
Combined Authority for funding of up to £24 million to
support infrastructure delivery at Gateshead Quays, forming part of
the Mayoral Development Zone, and enabling the regeneration of the
area through site preparation, public realm improvements and
infrastructure works.
 
RESOLVED:
i)                
Cabinet approved the submission of a Business Case to the North
East Combined Authority for up to £24 million for Gateshead
Quays Infrastructure Delivery.
ii)               
Cabinet delegated authority to the Strategic Director of Economy,
Innovation and Growth, in consultation with the Strategic Director,
Resources and Digital, and the Chief Legal Officer, to accept any
resulting grant and agree associated funding conditions.
 
The above decision was made for the following
reasons:
a)                
To bring forward the regeneration of Gateshead Quays.
b)                
To reaffirm the Council’s commitment to investing in the
local economy to provide sustainable opportunities for employment,
innovation and growth.
topline: The UK council has decided to submit a Business Case for funding to support infrastructure delivery at Gateshead Quays.

content:
Consideration was given to the report which
sought approval to submit a Stage 1 application to the National
Lottery Heritage Fund for the Tyne Derwent Way project, aimed at
securing funding to repair, conserve and enhance key heritage
assets, including Dunston Staiths,
improve access to the riverside, and deliver an engagement
programme connecting communities to local heritage and the natural
environment.
 
RESOLVED:
i)                
Cabinet approved the submission of a Stage 1 application to the
National Lottery Heritage Fund for the Tyne Derwent Way
project.
ii)               
Cabinet delegated authority to the Strategic Director of Economy,
Innovation and Growth to finalise the content of and submit the
Stage 1 application.
iii)             
Cabinet delegated authority to the Strategic Director of Economy,
Innovation and Growth, in consultation with the Strategic Director,
Resources and Digital, to accept any Stage 1 grant if the
application is successful.
 
The above decision was made for the following
reasons:
a)                
To ensure that the Council has funding to deliver its priorities as
identified in the Corporate Plan and the Council’s Capital
Programme.
topline: The Council has decided to secure funding for the Tyne Derwent Way project through a Stage 1 application to the National Lottery Heritage Fund.

content:
Consideration was given to the report which
set out the proposed Calendar of Meetings for the 2026–2027
municipal year, intended to enable effective planning of Council,
Cabinet, committee and board meetings and to support the orderly
conduct of the Council’s business.
 
RESOLVED:
i)                
Cabinet recommended that Council approves the Calendar of Meetings
for 2026–2027.
ii)               
Cabinet agreed that, as far as possible, meetings should not be
arranged during school holidays or on dates when religious
festivals may preclude attendance.
iii)             
Cabinet authorised the Chief Legal Officer to make any necessary
amendments to the Calendar of Meetings.
 
The above decision was made for the following
reasons:
a)                
To assist in the preparation of the Cabinet’s schedule of
decisions and to allow councillors, officers and partner
organisations to plan commitments in their diaries.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to approve the Calendar of Meetings for the 2026-2027 municipal year.

content:
Consideration was given to the report which
sought to note a change request to the approved costs for repairs
to the Maidens Walk Coal Drops, to accept grant funding from the
North East Combined Authority, and to delegate authority to
progress delivery of the repairs scheme to a Grade II listed
structure that forms a key part of the Gateshead Quays public realm
and regeneration proposals.
 
RESOLVED:
i)                
Cabinet agreed to accept the grant and delegated authority to the
Director of Finance to sign the grant funding agreement.
ii)               
Cabinet delegated authority to the Strategic Director of Economy,
Innovation and Growth to appoint the relevant Consultants for RIBA
Stages 2 to 4.
iii)             
Cabinet noted that approval would be sought at a later date,
through a separate Cabinet report, for the Council to enter into a
construction contract likely to exceed the constitutional
procurement threshold once a tender has been obtained at RIBA Stage
4.

 
The above decision was made for the following
reasons:
a)                
To enable delivery of the repairs scheme within scope, timescales
and budget.
b)                
To ensure that the Council has funding to deliver its priorities as
identified in the Corporate Plan and the Council’s Capital
Programme.
topline: The Council has decided to accept grant funding for repairs to a Grade II listed structure in Gateshead Quays.

content:
RESOLVED:
(i)              
That the press and public be excluded from the meeting during
consideration of the remaining business in accordance with
paragraph 3 of Schedule 12A to the Local Government Act 1972.
topline: The council has decided to exclude the press and public from a meeting

content:
Consideration was given to the latest
monitoring of the 2025/26 Capital Programme and Prudential
Indicators to 31 December 2025, including variances, proposed
financing, and compliance with the CIPFA Prudential Code.
 
RESOLVED:
i)                
That Cabinet agreed to recommend to Council approval of the
variations to the 2025/26 Capital Programme as set out in Appendix
2.
ii)               
That Cabinet agreed to recommend to Council the financing of the
revised programme as outlined in the report.
iii)             
That Cabinet confirmed to Council that the capital expenditure and
financing requirement indicators have been updated in line with the
amended budget and that no approved Prudential Indicators for
2025/26 have been breached.
 
The above decision was made for the following
reasons:
a)                
To ensure optimal use of the Council’s capital resources in
2025/26.
b)                
To accommodate changes to the Council’s in-year capital
expenditure plans.
c)                
To ensure performance has been assessed against the approved
Prudential Limits.
topline: The Council has decided to approve variations to the 2025/26 Capital Programme and confirm compliance with Prudential Indicators.

content:
Consideration was given to setting the council
tax base for 2026/27 for both the Borough of Gateshead and the
Parish of Lamesley, together with agreement of the business rates
forecast for 2026/27.
 
RESOLVED:
i)                
That Cabinet agreed, under the relevant Regulations, a council tax
base for Gateshead of 55,104.6 for 2026/27.
ii)               
That Cabinet agreed, under the relevant Regulations, a council tax
base for the Parish of Lamesley of 1,224.8 for 2026/27.
iii)             
That Cabinet agreed a business rates forecast of £47.705
million for 2026/27.
 
The above decision was made for the following
reasons:
a)                
To support the Council’s financial planning and budget
setting.
b)                
To set a council tax base and a business rates forecast for 2026/27
in line with statutory requirements.
topline: The Council has decided to set the council tax base and business rates forecast for 2026/27 for Gateshead and Lamesley

content:
Consideration was given to the third quarter
monitoring of the 2025/26 revenue budget, including projected
outturns for the General Fund and HRA, virements, and key pressures
and mitigations.
 
RESOLVED:
i)                
That Cabinet noted the Council’s revenue expenditure position
at the end of the third quarter, as detailed in Appendices 1 to
3.
 
The above decision was made for the following
reason:
a)                
To contribute to sound financial management and the
long?term financial sustainability of the
Council.
topline: The Council has decided to approve recommendations for the third quarter monitoring of the 2025/26 revenue budget.

content:
Consideration was given to adopting an updated
Corporate Complaints and Compliments Policy aligned to the Local
Government and Social Care Ombudsman’s Complaint Handling
Code and coordinated with the Housing Ombudsman’s Code,
including digital system improvements and appointment of a Member
Responsible for Complaints.
 
RESOLVED:
i)                
That Cabinet approved the revised Corporate Complaints and
Compliments Policy (Appendix 1).
ii)               
That Cabinet agreed that the ‘Member Responsible for
Complaints’ role continue to be undertaken by the Leader of
the Council.
 
The above decision was made for the following
reasons:
a)                
To ensure the Council complies with the requirements of the
Code.
b)                
To provide a coordinated and consistent complaint?handling process for Gateshead residents.
topline: The Council has decided to adopt an updated Corporate Complaints and Compliments Policy, with the Leader of the Council appointed as the 'Member Responsible for Complaints'.

content:
Consideration was given to making Local
Authority governor nominations in accordance with The School
Governance (Constitution) (England) Regulations, to maintain full
governing body membership.
 
RESOLVED:
i)                
That Cabinet approved the nomination for appointment or
re?appointment of a Local Authority Governor
as set out in Appendix 1.
ii)               
That Cabinet noted the term of office to be as determined by each
school’s Instrument of Government.
 
The above decision was made for the following
reason:
a)                
To ensure the School Governing Body has full membership.
topline: The UK council has decided to approve the appointment or re-appointment of a Local Authority Governor to maintain full governing body membership.

content:
Consideration was given to significantly
updating Gateshead’s Schools Forum Constitution and Guidance
to ensure representation is proportionate, compliant with the 2012
Regulations and DfE guidance, and reflective of changes in school
profiles and early years entitlements.
 
RESOLVED:
i)                
That Cabinet approved the updated Gateshead Schools Forum
Constitution and Guidance (Appendix 2).
 
The above decision was made for the following
reasons:
a)                
To ensure compliance with regulations and DfE guidance.
b)                
To ensure all Gateshead schools and young people are fairly
represented at Schools Forum.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to approve the updated Gateshead Schools Forum Constitution and Guidance to ensure fair representation for all schools and young people.

content:
Cllr M Gannon withdrew from the meeting for
consideration of this item. Cllr G Haley took over as Chair.
 
Consideration was given to a report, presented
in the absence of the press and public, on proposed arrangements
relating to the Council’s shareholding in Newcastle
International Airport.
 
RESOLVED – That, having considered a
report in the absence of the press and public pursuant to Schedule
12A of the Local Government Act 1972 (as amended), Cabinet:
i)                
That authority be delegated to the Leader of the Council to
provide, on behalf of the Council, the necessary shareholder
consent in connection with proposed changes to the ownership
structure of the Airport’s private sector partner.

 
The above decision was made for the following
reason:
a)            
To support the continued development of Newcastle International
Airport and its contribution to regional connectivity and economic
growth.
topline: The Council has decided to approve recommendations for proposed changes to the ownership structure of Newcastle International Airport.

content:
Consideration was given to the update on the
Council’s Budget 2026/27, including the implications of the
Provisional Local Government Finance Settlement, the assumptions
within the Medium Term Financial Strategy, and the proposal to
commence internal consultation with employees and trade unions on
the draft revenue savings proposals for 2026/27 as part of the
budget planning process. The report also outlined the statutory
redundancy consultation associated with workforce budget proposals
and provided an overview of the current financial position, funding
uncertainties and the next steps prior to confirmation of the final
settlement in February 2026.
 
RESOLVED:
i)                
That the update to the funding position, including the outcome of
the Provisional Local Government Finance Settlement set out in
Appendix 1, be noted.
ii)               
That the update on the 2026/27 budget planning process be
noted.
iii)             
That the response to the Government consultation on the Provisional
Local Government Finance Settlement included at Appendix 2 be
noted.
iv)             
That approval be given to the commencement of internal consultation
with employees and trade unions on workforce related budget
proposals for 2026/27 as detailed in Appendix 3.
 
The above decision was made for the following
reasons:

a)    
To contribute to the good financial management practice of the
Council.

b)    
To assist the financial sustainability of the Council over the
medium to long term.

c)    
To support delivery of the Council’s Corporate Plan
priorities and the Thrive objectives.
topline: The Council has decided to update the Budget for 2026/27 and commence internal consultation on revenue savings proposals, with recommendations approved.

content:
Consideration was given to the allocation of
the Pride in Place Impact Fund, with the aim of empowering local
communities to improve places and spaces that matter to them. The
report sought Cabinet approval for a suite of projects designed to
invest in community facilities, enhance public spaces, and
revitalise high streets and town centres, supporting Gateshead
Council’s corporate priorities and the Thrive pledges.
 
RESOLVED:
i)                
Cabinet agreed to the proposed projects to be taken forward to
deliver the £1.5m Pride in Place Impact Fund funding
identified in Appendix 3 of the report.

 
The above decision was made for the following
reasons:
a)            
To enable successful delivery of the Pride in Place Impact
Fund.
b)            
To enable successful delivery of activity in Gateshead that will
contribute to local priorities and the Council’s Corporate
Plan.
topline: The Gateshead Council has decided to approve recommendations for the allocation of the Pride in Place Impact Fund.

content:
Councillor M Hall excused
themselves from the meeting for consideration of this item
following a declaration of interest.
 
Proposal to Declare Derwent
Park Bowling Green and Pavilion and Clara Vale Recreation Ground
Surplus to Council Requirements and to Grant Community Asset
Transfer Leases
Consideration was given to the
proposal to declare Derwent Park Bowling Green and Pavilion, and
Clara Vale Recreation Ground Cricket Field, Football Pitch,
Pavilion and Store, surplus to Council requirements, and to grant
35-year leases under the Community Asset Transfer policy. The
purpose was to rationalise assets, support community-led
regeneration, and empower local organisations to manage these
facilities.
 
RESOLVED:
i)                
Cabinet approved the recommendations set out in
Appendices 1-2 of the report.

 
The above decision was made for
the following reasons:
a)            
To manage resources and rationalise the
Council’s assets in line with the Corporate Asset Strategy
and Management Plan.
b)            
To further develop partnerships and asset transfer
arrangements in line with Gateshead Playing Pitch
Strategy.
topline: The Council has decided to declare Derwent Park Bowling Green and Pavilion and Clara Vale Recreation Ground surplus to requirements and grant 35-year leases under the Community Asset Transfer policy.

content:
Consideration was given to the
procurement and award of contracts listed in Appendix 2, with the
intention of ensuring efficient and effective delivery of Council
services. The report provided an overview of planned procurement
activity, progress on previously approved contracts, and updates on
awarded contracts, in line with the National Procurement Policy
Statement and the Procurement Act 2023.
 
RESOLVED:
i)                
The Service Director, Financial Management was
authorised to:
·       
invite or negotiate tenders
·       
conduct other procurement processes,
·       
complete relevant processes in respect of the
contracts listed in Appendix 2
·       
award contracts to the tenderers submitting the most
economically advantageous tenders in accordance with Contract
Procedure Rules
ii)               
Cabinet will continue to receive an updated report
twice per year.
iii)             
Following Cabinet approval, the procurement activity
set out in Appendix 2 will form the basis of the Council’s
Procurement Pipeline and be published on the Council’s
internet page. Contracts over £2m will also be published on
the Central Digital Platform in accordance with the Procurement Act
2023.
 
The above decision was made for
the following reasons:
a)                
To enable the procurement of goods, works and
services required for the efficient and effective delivery of
services.
b)                
To enable Cabinet to be updated with progress and
changes to the procurement forward plan.
c)                
To comply with the National Procurement Policy
Statement and Procurement Act.
topline: The Council has decided to approve recommendations for procurement and award of contracts to ensure efficient delivery of services.

content:
Cabinet considered a report
regarding the appointment of consultants to support the Metro
Riverside regeneration scheme.
 
RESOLVED – That, having
considered a report in the absence of the press and public pursuant
to Schedule 12A of the Local Government Act 1972 (as amended),
Cabinet:
i)                
Agreed that Mace be appointed, via negotiated tender
through the Scape Framework, to produce an Outline Business Case
and Masterplan for the Metro Riverside scheme.
ii)               
Agreed the Council enter into a Collaboration and
Funding Agreement with The MetroCentre
Partnership to establish joint governance arrangements and to
ensure that 50% of the costs can be recovered from the MetroCentre Partnership.
 
The above decision was made for
the following reason:
a)            
To enable the production of a Business Case and
submission of a bid to UK Government funding to deliver the Metro
Riverside scheme
topline: The Council has decided to appoint consultants to support the Metro Riverside regeneration scheme.

content:
Consideration was given to a report regarding
the conversion of Council garages at Penrith Grove into new Council
housing.
 
RESOLVED – That, having considered a
report in the absence of the press and public pursuant to Schedule
12A of the Local Government Act 1972 (as amended), Cabinet:
i)                
Agreed that the Council enter a contract with HUSK for the delivery
of five two-bedroom bungalows at Penrith Grove.
ii)               
That authority be delegated to the Strategic Director, Housing,
Environment and Healthy Communities, and the Strategic Director,
Resources and Digital, in consultation with the Leader, to agree a
maximum 10% increase to the contract price to account for any
unforeseen cost uplift.
 
The above decision was made for the following
reason:
a)                
To enable the conversion of garages at Penrith Grove into new
affordable housing, supporting the Council’s Housing Strategy
and the sustainability of the Housing Revenue Account Business
Plan.
topline: The Council has decided to convert garages at Penrith Grove into new affordable housing, supporting the Council's Housing Strategy.

content:
Consideration was given to the
revised Gateshead Compact, an agreement between the Council,
Voluntary Community and Social Enterprise (VCSE) sector, and public
sector partners to work together to agreed standards and shared
objectives. The purpose was to strengthen relationships, ensure
sustainability of the VCSE sector, and maximise collective impact
for Gateshead communities.
 
RESOLVED:
i)                
Cabinet approved the revised Gateshead
Compact.

 
The above decision was made for
the following reasons:
 
a)            
To enhance the relationship between the VCSE sector
and the Council.
b)            
To ensure a sustainable and resilient VCSE
sector.
c)            
To maximise collective impact and resources to
improve services for Gateshead communities and outcomes for local
people.
topline: The Council has decided to approve the revised Gateshead Compact, strengthening relationships and maximizing impact for Gateshead communities.

content:
Councillor A Douglas remained present for
consideration of this item following a declaration of interest.
 
Consideration was given to the nomination of
Local Authority Governors to schools seeking to retain their Local
Authority governor, in accordance with The School Governance
(Constitution) (England) Regulations. The purpose was to ensure
governing bodies have full membership and appropriate
representation.
 
RESOLVED:
i)                
Cabinet approved the nomination for appointment/reappointment of a
Local Authority Governor.
ii)               
Term of office as determined by the schools’ Instrument of
Government.
 
The above decision was made for the following
reasons:
a)            
To ensure the School Governing Body has full membership.
topline: The Council has decided to approve the nomination of Local Authority Governors to schools seeking to retain their Local Authority governor.

content:
Consideration was given to a
report regarding the delivery of Phase One of the Local Electric
Vehicle Infrastructure (LEVI) programme.
 
RESOLVED – That, having
considered a report in the absence of the press and public pursuant
to Schedule 12A of the Local Government Act 1972 (as amended),
Cabinet approved:
i)                
That the Council enter into a tripartite contract
with the supplier and North East Combined Authority (NECA) for the
delivery of LEVI Phase One.
ii)               
That the financial and operational implications for
Gateshead Council be noted.
iii)             
That approval be given for electric vehicle chargers
to be installed on Council property and land. iv) That authority be
delegated to the Interim Service Director for Climate Change,
Compliance, Planning & Transport, in consultation with the
Cabinet Member for Environment and Transport, to investigate and,
where appropriate, install electric vehicle charge points at
locations not specifically identified in Phase One.
 
The above decision was made for
the following reason:
a)            
To enable NECA to appoint the chosen supplier and
commence installation of electric vehicle infrastructure in
Gateshead; to permit use of Council property for EV chargers; and
to allow flexibility in the location of charge points in response
to emerging needs.
topline: The Gateshead Council has decided to approve the delivery of Phase One of the Local Electric Vehicle Infrastructure (LEVI) programme.

content:
Consideration was given to the
annual Infrastructure Funding Statement (IFS), which details
financial contributions secured through the Community
Infrastructure Levy (CIL) and Section 106 agreements for off-site
infrastructure works and affordable housing. The report sought
approval to publish the updated IFS on the Council’s website,
ensuring transparency and compliance with statutory
requirements.
 
RESOLVED:
i)                
Cabinet approved the current strategy for the CIL
Strategic Fund.
ii)               
Cabinet approved the IFS set out in Appendix 2 for
publication by the end of December 2025.
 
The above decision was made for
the following reasons:
a)            
To comply with CIL Regulations.
b)            
To continue to ensure that developer contributions
received are published and spent in a transparent
manner.
topline: The Council has decided to approve the annual Infrastructure Funding Statement and the current strategy for the CIL Strategic Fund.

content:
Consideration was given to the
mid-year update on the Local Transport Plan (LTP) Capital
Programme, summarising progress and changes to integrated transport
and maintenance schemes. The report included indicative programmes
for 2026/27 to support forward planning and sought approval for
revised and future programmes.
 
RESOLVED:
i)                
Cabinet approved the revised programmes for 2025/26
as set out in Appendices A and B, noting the need for ongoing
review.
ii)               
Cabinet authorised the Service Director, Highways
and Waste to award relevant works under the Highways, Drainage and
Street Lighting Maintenance Contract.
iii)             
Cabinet authorised the Interim Service Director,
Climate Change, Compliance, Planning & Transport to make
changes to the approved programme following consultation with the
Cabinet Member for Environment and Transport.
iv)             
Cabinet approved the indicative integrated transport
and maintenance programmes for 2026/27 as a basis for future
planning.
 
The above decision was made for
the following reason:
a)            
To enable the design and implementation of transport
schemes in support of the North East Transport Plan and the
Council’s policy objectives.
topline: The Council has decided to approve revised and future programmes for the Local Transport Plan Capital Programme, including indicative programmes for 2026/27.
